## Part A - Arithmetic Operator
```{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5

a + b
a - b
a * b
a / b

a %% b
a %/% b

2 ^10
```
**Question #1:**
17 %/% 5 gives 3 (how many full times 5 fits in 17) and 17 %% 5 gives 2 (the leftover part). Together they rebuild 17 because (3 × 5) + 2 = 17. Converting the leftover part (2 ÷ 5 = 0.4) and adding it to 3 gives 3.4 (17 / 5), which is the full decimal answer.

**Question #2:**
I predicted 10 %% 3 is 1 and 10 %/% 3 is 3. This was correct because 3 fits into 10 three whole times with 1 remainder.

## Part B - Basic Data Types
```{r}
 x <- 42
 y <- 42L
 z <- "42"
 w <- TRUE
 v <- 3 + 2i
 
 typeof(x)
 typeof(y)
 typeof(z)
 typeof(w)
 typeof(v)
 
 class(x)
 class(y)
 class(z)
 class(w)
 class(v) 

 
 mode(x)
 mode(y)
 mode(z)
 mode(w)
 mode(v)
```
**Question #3:**
typeof(x) returns "double" because R stores numbers as decimals by default. typeof(y) returns "integer" because adding L to 42L tells R to save it specifically as a whole number without decimals.


**Question #4:**
Yes. typeof() tells you how R stores the data, while class() tells you how R handles it. For example, a factor has typeof() of "integer" because R stores categories using numbers, but its class() is "factor".

as.numeric (bad_string)

## Part D - Strings, paste(), and paste0()

```{r}
first_name <- "Mariane Jamilah"
last_name <- "Carias"
print(first_name)
print(last_name)
cat(first_name, last_name) 

full_name <- paste(first_name, last_name)
full_name
paste0(first_name,last_name)

paste0(first_name,last_name, sep = "-")

age <- 21
paste0(full_name, "is", age, "years old.")
```

**Question #7:**
paste() automatically adds a space between text because its default separator is sep = " ". paste0() joins text with no space at all because its default is sep = "".

**Question #8:**
No, it didn't cause an error. paste0() automatically converts numbers to text behind the scenes before combining them, which works just like as.character() in Part C.
